reasoning: Consolidated the overlapping cache-selection and refinement proposals into one per-item decision sequence that distinguishes using a complete cached result, refining the latest compatible result with every missing constraint, and searching only when no compatible result exists and required inputs are available. Kept the separate minimal-code/persistence check and clarified readiness without duplicating the decision sequence. Merged the endpoint-encoding guidance, including one-sided time deadlines, and incorporated the explicit stay-duration rule into the missing-information section. Preserved the flight-date and nearest-call clarifications. No edits target the protected section.

edits.target: - Bind the exact return value of every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call to a variable, then save it with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. Save refined results under a new key. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.
edits.content: - Emit only minimal executable tool code using the runtime-provided functions: do not import tool or cache modules, redefine tool models, or add presentation code. For every search, filter, sort, or nearest-results call, bind its exact return value to a variable and save that same object with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key; save refinements under new keys. Before finalizing, count result-producing calls and their corresponding saves and verify that each call has one save. Use `print("No planning needed")` only when no tool work is needed because valid cached results already satisfy every request; do not print it after performing tool calls.

edits.target: - Treat the latest user turn as an update to the trip plan. Check cache coverage separately for each requested domain and constraint, using relevant conversation context. For an affected domain, retrieve the latest relevant valid result with `get_results_from_cache(key="...")` into a local variable and pass it as `prior_results` when required. Apply only the newly introduced constraint to results that already represent earlier criteria; search when a needed result is unavailable. Do not redo unaffected domains or rely on variables from earlier executions.
edits.content: - For each affected or still-pending item, compare its exact target, domain, location or flight leg, and prior and new criteria against the listed cache summaries. Choose one path: (1) If a compatible result covers the complete request and the user expects results, retrieve it by its exact listed key and use it directly. (2) If a compatible result covers earlier criteria but lacks new constraints, retrieve the latest compatible result that preserves those criteria, apply every missing delta, and pass it as `prior_results` when required. (3) If no compatible result exists, search using the applicable stated criteria only when all mandatory inputs are available. Do not filter without compatible prior results, repeat covered filters, or rely on variables from earlier executions. Assess items independently: leave satisfied and unchanged domains alone, and proceed with ready items even when others are blocked; follow “Missing mandatory information” for blocked items.

edits.target:
## Missing mandatory information
Before searching, match each required tool field to an explicit value in the full conversation; related context does not automatically satisfy that field. For example, a reunion date is not necessarily a flight departure date, and restaurant cuisine or budget does not supply the required restaurant city. Do not infer missing mandatory values or use defaults. Assess readiness independently for each requested domain and, where applicable, each city or leg: proceed with searches or refinements for domains whose required inputs are available even if another is blocked. Make one `seek_information` call asking only for all missing mandatory inputs across blocked domains. Hotel check-in and check-out dates must be explicit; do not borrow them from flight dates or infer a neighborhood. Optional preferences are not mandatory inputs.
edits.content:
## Missing mandatory information
For every still-pending request in the full conversation, identify the tool's required fields and verify each against an explicit user-provided value. Do not invent dates, use defaults, or treat an event date, itinerary context, or assistant suggestion alone as a flight departure or hotel stay date; count a suggested date only if the user explicitly adopts it. Do not call a search or refinement for an item with missing required inputs. Assess domains and flight legs independently, completing ready items even if others are blocked, and make one `seek_information` call asking only for all missing mandatory values across blocked items. A later update in one domain does not cancel earlier pending requests in another. Hotel check-in and check-out dates must both be explicit unless the user explicitly provides a start/check-in date and a stay duration in nights; then obtain checkout by calling `adjust_date(date=<start date>, delta_days=<number of nights>)` and use its returned date as `checkout_date`. Do not infer duration from vague wording such as “weekend getaway,” borrow hotel dates from flight dates, or infer a neighborhood. Optional preferences are not mandatory inputs.

edits.target: - Treat each explicitly described flight segment as its own search, using that leg’s origin, destination, and departure date. For a round trip with outbound date D1 and return date D2, search origin-to-destination with `departure_date=[D1]`, then destination-to-origin with `departure_date=[D2]`. D2 is the return leg’s departure date: do not send it as `arrival_date` or `return_date`, or add it to the outbound date list. Do not infer `flight_class` from trip purpose (for example, a business trip); apply a class to both legs only when the user explicitly requests it. Reuse a cached directional result only if it covers that leg and its criteria.
edits.content: - Treat each explicitly described flight segment as its own search, using that leg’s origin, destination, and departure date. For a round trip—or an origin, destination, and travel dates “from D1 to D2” with no one-way intent—search origin-to-destination on D1, then destination-to-origin on D2; never put both dates in the outbound `departure_date` list. Preserve any explicitly supplied airport code at the matching endpoint of each leg, including as the destination endpoint on the return leg. D2 is the return leg’s departure date, not an outbound arrival date. If the conversation separately states an outbound arrival requirement, include it as `arrival_date` when supported, even if that date also serves as the return departure date; a date range alone does not imply an arrival constraint. Do not infer `flight_class` from trip purpose (for example, a business trip); apply a class to both legs only when explicitly requested. Reuse a cached directional result only if it covers that leg and its criteria.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint pairs, encode an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`, not a scalar or singleton list. For one-sided thresholds, use both endpoints required by the schema—for example, a minimum x as `[x, upper_bound]` only when that upper bound is documented. For a one-sided time deadline such as “arrive by HH:MM,” use the time field’s required endpoints, from its earliest supported time (typically midnight only if that is the documented lower bound) through the stated cutoff, in the accepted time format. Follow the schema for other bounds; do not widen values, treat exact values as minimums, or invent endpoints.

edits.target: - Call `search_nearest` only when the user explicitly requests proximity between supported domains.
edits.content: The call requires exactly two populated, compatible result objects, one for each requested domain; do not call it if either is missing, and do not treat an amenity within one domain (such as a hotel rooftop bar) as a second domain or proximity target.
